title: Rafael Calderon Fournier Wins Presidency for PUSC
notes: Calderon won February 4, 1990 election with ~52% vs PLN's Carlos Manuel Castillo. PUSC affiliation confirmed.

title: Oscar Arias Awarded Nobel Peace Prize Legacy Shapes Foreign Policy
notes: Nobel Prize was awarded in 1987, not 1990. Event describes 1990s legacy, not a discrete 1990 event. Year is plausible for ongoing foreign policy framing but not a verifiable dated occurrence.

title: Costa Rica Ratifies UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
notes: UNFCCC was opened for signature June 1992 and entered into force March 1994. Costa Rica ratified in 1994, not 1992. Year off by 2.

title: Jose Maria Figueres Olsen Elected President
notes: Figueres (PLN) won February 6, 1994 election. Son of Jose Figueres Ferrer confirmed.

title: Forestry Law Establishes Payment for Environmental Services
notes: Forestry Law No. 7575 enacted in 1996, created PES programme via FONAFIFO. Globally recognized model confirmed.

title: Constitutional Amendment Bans Presidential Reelection
notes: The reelection ban originates from the 1969 constitutional amendment, not 1997. A 1997 law (No. 7675) existed but did not establish the reelection ban. Materially wrong attribution of year and cause.

title: Miguel Angel Rodriguez Wins Presidency
notes: Rodriguez (PUSC) won February 1, 1998 with 46.96% vs PLN's 44.56%. Pro-market privatization agenda confirmed.

title: Combo ICE Protests Block Telecom Privatization
notes: March 2000 nationwide protests against 'Combo ICE' bill. Bill withdrawn from Congress. Described as most significant social protest in recent Costa Rican history.

title: Two-Party System Collapses in Historic Election
notes: PAC won 14 of 57 seats (21.9%). Abel Pacheco (PUSC) won unprecedented runoff. Confirmed as beginning of end of two-party system.

title: Supreme Court Overturns Presidential Reelection Ban
notes: Constitutional Chamber ruled 5-2 in April 2003, striking down the 1969 amendment. Cleared path for Arias second term.

title: Three Former Presidents Accused of Corruption
notes: Calderon, Rodriguez, and Figueres all faced corruption charges in 2004 related to CAJA and Alcatel bribes. PUSC devastation confirmed.

title: Oscar Arias Wins Razor-Thin Presidential Election
notes: Arias won with 40.92% vs Solis's 39.80%, margin of ~18,169 votes. Month-long recount confirmed. Polarization over CAFTA confirmed.

title: CAFTA Approved in First-Ever National Referendum
notes: Referendum held October 7, 2007. Approved with 51.56% in favor. First national referendum in Costa Rica confirmed.

title: Costa Rica Switches Diplomatic Recognition from Taiwan to China
notes: Arias announced switch June 6, 2007. First Central American country to do so. ~60 years of ties with Taiwan confirmed.

title: CAFTA Implementation Legislation Package Enacted
notes: 13 implementation laws required post-referendum. Opened telecom and insurance to competition. Broadly confirmed.

title: Costa Rica Achieves Carbon Neutrality Pledge
notes: The carbon neutrality pledge (target year 2021) was made in 2007, not 2009. Year off by 2.

title: Laura Chinchilla Elected First Female President
notes: Chinchilla (PLN) won February 7, 2010 with 46.76%. First female president of Costa Rica confirmed.

title: Nicaragua Occupies Disputed Isla Portillos Territory
notes: Nicaragua dredged San Juan River and entered Isla Portillos October 2010. Costa Rica filed ICJ suit November 2010. Confirmed.

title: ICJ Orders Provisional Measures in Nicaragua Border Dispute
notes: ICJ Order of March 8, 2011 directed both parties to refrain from sending personnel to disputed territory. Confirmed.

title: China-Funded National Stadium Inaugurated
notes: Stadium inaugurated March 26, 2011. Cost ~$100-115M. Built by Anhui Foreign Economic Construction. Gift linked to 2007 diplomatic switch confirmed.

title: Major Earthquake Strikes Nicoya Peninsula
notes: Mw 7.6 earthquake struck Nicoya Peninsula on September 5, 2012. Described as strongest in over a century. Minimal casualties due to building codes confirmed.

title: Constitutional Court Voids Chinchilla Concession Mining Ban
notes: Could not confirm a specific 2013 Constitutional Chamber ruling voiding a mining ban. The 2010 open-pit mining moratorium is documented but no specific 2013 court voidance found.

title: Luis Guillermo Solis Wins Landslide Anti-Corruption Election
notes: Solis (PAC) won April 6, 2014 runoff with 77.8%. First non-PLN/PUSC president since 1948 confirmed.

title: ICJ Rules in Favor of Costa Rica in Nicaragua Border Case
notes: ICJ judgment December 16, 2015 confirmed Costa Rica sovereignty over Isla Portillos. Compensation amount determined in 2018 ($378,890.59), not 2015. Core sovereignty ruling in 2015 correct.

title: Costa Rica Achieves Over 98 Percent Renewable Electricity
notes: Costa Rica ran on 100% renewables for 299 consecutive days in 2015. Primarily hydropower. Global attention confirmed.

title: Pension System Reform Debate Intensifies
notes: Ongoing fiscal pressure on CCSS pension system is well-documented generally, but no specific 2016 actuarial report or legislative event could be confirmed.

title: Inter-American Court Orders Costa Rica to Legalize Same-Sex Marriage
notes: Advisory Opinion OC-24/17 issued November 24, 2017 (published January 9, 2018). Binding on OAS Convention signatories including Costa Rica. Confirmed.

title: Carlos Alvarado Wins Presidency in Marriage Equality Election
notes: Alvarado (PAC) won April 1, 2018 runoff with 60.74% vs Fabricio Alvarado (evangelical, PRN) 39.26%. Same-sex marriage defining issue confirmed.

title: Massive Public Sector Strike Against Fiscal Reform
notes: Strike began September 10, 2018. Sources confirm approximately 80 days duration. Described as largest in 20 years. '138 billion colones in losses' figure unconfirmed in sources but duration and scale verified.

title: Fiscal Strengthening Law Enacted Despite Protests
notes: Ley 9635 (Fortalecimiento de las Finanzas Publicas) passed December 3, 2018. Replaced sales tax with VAT. Deficit ~5-6% of GDP confirmed.

title: ICJ Awards Costa Rica Compensation in Nicaragua Dispute
notes: ICJ judgment February 2, 2018 awarded $378,890.59 total to Costa Rica. Amount matches exactly.

title: Costa Rica Joins OECD as First Central American Member
notes: Costa Rica formally joined OECD on May 25, 2021, not 2019. Year off by 2. The accession process was ongoing in 2019 but membership was not granted until 2021.

title: Same-Sex Marriage Legalized
notes: Same-sex marriage became legal May 26, 2020. First in Central America. Court-mandated deadline expiry mechanism confirmed.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Devastates Tourism Economy
notes: Tourism ~8% of GDP, severely hit by COVID-19. Phased reopening approach confirmed.

title: Anti-IMF Loan Protests and Road Blockades
notes: Protests began late September 2020 against $1.75B IMF loan. Multiple road blockades confirmed. Government withdrew proposal October 4, 2020.

title: Tropical Storm Eta and Hurricane Iota Cause Severe Flooding
notes: Eta and Iota struck November 2020, causing flooding and landslides across Costa Rica. Confirmed.

title: Costa Rica Formally Joins OECD
notes: Formally joined May 25, 2021 as 38th member. First Central American nation. Confirmed.

title: Public Employment Framework Law Enacted
notes: Marco de Empleo Publico passed to standardize public sector pay. OECD accession condition confirmed. Union opposition confirmed.

title: Rodrigo Chaves Wins Presidency as Anti-Establishment Populist
notes: Chaves (PSDP) won April 3, 2022 runoff with 53% vs Figueres 47%. Former World Bank economist. Anti-establishment framing confirmed.

title: Chaves Declares State of Emergency Over Cost of Living
notes: Chaves declared state of emergency in May 2022 due to ransomware/cyber attacks, not cost of living. Materially wrong stated cause.

title: Chaves Jaguar Plan Clashes with Legislature and Comptroller
notes: Chaves's Plan Jaguar and conflicts with legislature and Comptroller General are well-documented. Blocking of bills confirmed.

title: Eco-Tourism Sector Recovers to Record Visitor Numbers
notes: Tourism rebounded post-COVID surpassing pre-pandemic levels. Eco-tourism model and 25% territory under parks broadly confirmed.

title: Chaves Administration Faces Press Freedom Criticism
notes: International press freedom orgs documented Chaves's confrontational rhetoric against media. Derogatory language toward journalists confirmed.

title: Nicaragua Migration Surge Strains Social Services
notes: Large Nicaraguan asylum seeker population in Costa Rica documented by Freedom House and others. 200,000+ figure is plausible per sources.

title: Costa Rica Hosts Transit Migration from South America
notes: Costa Rica as transit country for South American migrants is a documented ongoing issue, but the specific 2025 bilateral agreements mentioned could not be confirmed with web sources available.
